body.text: If you know me, you know this has been a long time coming.

bloks.name: WORD MEME
bloks.title: AlgoSpeak: Fluent in Censorship
bloks.dek: The coded language of digital survival.

body.text: Algospeak (n.) 💬 A coded way of speaking online — swapping or altering words so algorithms don’t flag, censor, or down-rank what you say. 🧩

body.alt: Two faces in profile, mouths covered by a yellow tape that reads AlgoSpeak

body.text: Is “AlgoSpeak” just cultural language evolution or a sign of a wrong turn?
Instead of saying “suicide,” they say “unalive.” Instead of “sex,” they say “seggs.” 🔄
Because somewhere along the line, we stopped talking to each other — and started talking around the platforms. 🌐
The elephant in the room
Are we being censored — or just curated?

bloks.name: FIND YOUR EDGE
bloks.title: Vinh Giang: Five Phrases That Rewire Conversation
bloks.dek: Small lines that make people feel heard.

body.text: Vinh Giang is all about helping people become better communicators. Here’s one that stood out this week.

body.cap: Vinh Giang: five phrases. Watch on YouTube.
body.alt: Vinh Giang demonstrating conversation phrases

items: “Tell me more” — shows curiosity and makes others feel valued.
“That’s such an interesting way to look at it” — validates without judgment.
“That must have been such a big moment for you” — acknowledges emotion.
“What do you love most about it?” — uncovers passion.
“I see where you’re coming from” — creates psychological safety through empathy.

bloks.name: CHAIN REACTION
bloks.title: What Is a Cypherpunk, Anyway?
bloks.dek: Crypto 101: the privacy punks of the network age.

body.alt: Anime character with a raised eyebrow: HMM?

body.text: Welcome to crypto
So, what is a Cypherpunk? If the 1970s punk scene tore down the stage to build its own, the cypherpunks did the same — only in code.
They’re the ones who looked at a growing internet and said, “Cool, but who’s watching?” Then they built the locks, the tunnels, and the currencies that let people move freely through digital space.
Think of them as the privacy punks of the network age — DIY technologists who believed freedom required encryption, not permission. Their rebellion wasn’t with guitars, but with math.
Like the original punks, they weren’t waiting for the system to change; they just started building a new one in its shadow.
Not exclusive to writing code — the Cypherpunk movement is a mindset about how people think, act, and align with a certain kind of progress.

bloks.name: STORY BEAT
bloks.title: Scanning Barcodes Like Life Depends On It
bloks.dek: Episode 1: will, poise, and quiet rebellion.

body.text: Cameras watch him. Co-workers micro-manage him. Managers hunt for new ways he can perpetually “improve.” All this — for the privilege of going into debt.
It’s a story about will, poise, and quiet rebellion.
Sometimes the only way to get what you want is to rely completely on yourself — to depend on no one.
Either the crowd decides who you are, or you decide who you are. Who prevails?

body.alt: Episode 1 of the Apron Worker series

body.text: Andrew Rousso nails that balance of smart and unhinged. It even takes a left turn at the end, but compared to his usual dives, this one’s practically a palate cleanser.

bloks.name: MUSIC FLOW
bloks.title: SALES — “Renee”
bloks.dek: Found in a freezing parking lot. My secret emo side.

body.text: Back in my car-selling days at Mercedes (less than a year ago 😂), I found this song.

The buyer and I had just agreed on a deal after hours — around 9 p.m. The expectation was to prep the cars ourselves, which meant heading out into the freezing Pacific Northwest night to find it, fill it with gas, and wash it inside and out.

I sprint around back — because that’s what you do when you’ve got ten minutes before your guest walks out of finance. I get into the car’s icy interior. The lot is stark and quiet, street lamps refracting off windows, hundreds of cars surrounding me. I turn the key; the dash lights up.
And there it is — a soft guitar riff cuts through the cold.
The song’s already playing on the radio, and somehow it just… gets me.
A calm, surreal dopamine rush. Like, okay, someone out there understands.
The song’s about a moment that “took too long to get at me,” which just fits. It’s that don’t-waste-my-time energy in music form.

SALES performing Renee live

bloks.name: OFF THE PATH
bloks.title: Heads-Up Before You Watch: DoesTheDogDie.com
bloks.dek: Check a movie for spoilers you’d rather avoid.

body.text: Did you know there’s a site that tells you whether a dog dies in a movie or show? It’s called DoesTheDogDie.com.

body.alt: A wireframe globe under a red radar sweep

body.text: The mobile ads are brutal and make it clunky to use, but the core idea is surprisingly useful: you can check a title for dog-related spoilers and other trigger warnings if certain scenes hit you hard and you’d rather avoid them.
Pretty wild, huh?

bloks.name: WALL OF SOMMI
bloks.title: A Secret Best Kept
bloks.dek: Less a crypto channel, more internet theater.

body.text: Your Friend Sommi is a guy talking to a camera about financial markets and crypto. But really — it’s more like internet theater.
Somehow, this one guy with a camera has enough presence that you start referring to his videos as “episodes”… of his… “show.”

body.alt: Sommi in a red-and-white knit hat at a microphone

body.text: I had no idea what he was saying when I first started watching. I’d play it in the background, catching a few words here and there through his Australian accent.
There are naturally recurring themes and phrases that take his efforts into cult territory:

Sommi plays his “pumpy G music” as a topic transition interlude, reminds the viewer he’s studying financial markets “18 hours a day,” and delivers “the highest-value content in crypto — it’s not even close.”
This is my shrine to Sommi. I’ll share highlight clips here.

body.alt: Sommi in a knit hat

bloks.name: SPORTS TALK
bloks.title: Bronx Bomb by Bonds, and I Can Still Hear the Haters

body.text: What pulls us toward sports — and life — is that you can’t recreate the moment. Each second challenges you to respond, to feel, to decide how much it matters. It quietly asks: Do you love this enough?
We witness greatness and try to appreciate it, but most of the time we don’t know how. Sometimes, we don’t even realize how great something truly is until it’s gone.
Enter Barry Bonds.
I can still hear the haters — they’ve become a kind of muse. Every insult just deepens the myth. The more they try to tear him down, the larger he looms.
Centuries from now, they’ll still be telling stories about Barry Bonds. And I doubt he’ll be any more understood then than he is now — which is to say, barely at all.
But as they say: Real ones know.
